coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Piers 38 & 40
record.distance_note: Piers 38 and 40, at the foot of King St/Townsend St (89 King St), sit about 420-460m north of Mission Rock's own tracked boundary (Pier 48/50), just north of and adjacent to South Beach Harbor.

how_to_comment.channel: Port of San Francisco project page

record.summary: A long-stalled Port of San Francisco redevelopment of Piers 38 and 40, led by San Francisco Waterfront Partners (an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners). The original 2021 Exclusive Negotiating Agreement expired in 2023 after missed performance dates; in April 2026 the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA giving the developer a 12-month "Evaluation Period" to rework the project's scope and financing. No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's last_verified date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- two hand-traced deck outlines (Pier 38 and Pier 40) from satellite imagery, accurate to a few metres at best, not a surveyed footprint and not a Port or Assessor geometry. Each is drawn as a parallelogram (opposite edges parallel). They cover the main decks only: the Pier 38 bulkhead building along the Embarcadero, the narrow dock off Pier 40's east end, and any pile-supported aprons are left out. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or site-plan figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for this Port pier facility (confirmed: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset, acdm-wktn, has no PIER-numbered street_name entries). No Port GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available. CORRECTED 2026-09-30: the box's location is now the union of OpenStreetMap's own two named building entries for the piers -- 'Pier 40' (way 104599990, bounding box lat 37.7815294-37.7819100, lon -122.3870563--122.3855684) and 'Pier 38' (way 104599982, bounding box lat 37.7818929-37.7829023, lon -122.3879887--122.3847049), both confirmed via OpenStreetMap Nominatim on 2026-09-30 -- not a traced footprint of either building, just their combined location, since no Port GIS figure or site plan exists to trace from. CORRECTED 2026-10-10: the outline is now two hand-traced deck outlines (Pier 38 to the north, Pier 40 to the south) on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29 per docs/satellite-imagery.md), placed by calibrating against the previous box's known corners and corrected corner by corner in review with the owner. Still no Assessor parcel, Port GIS layer or site-plan figure to trace from.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Port pier facility; not on the Assessor's secured roll (data.sf.gov acdm-wktn has no PIER-numbered parcels near this site).
notes.regulatory_context: Developer: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP). Original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement: Port Commission Resolution 21-10 (2021-02-23), expired 2023-03-15 for missed performance dates. PWP separately owed the Port over $980,000 in back rent on three unrelated leases (Pier 28, two Agriculture Building suites), unpaid since it vacated them 2024-01-31. On 2026-04-28 the Port Commission adopted a Settlement Agreement (Resolution 26-21: PWP to pay $720,000 over 3 years, with the remainder of the debt forgiven on compliance) and an Amended and Restated ENA (Resolution 26-22: a 12-month 'Evaluation Period' to explore value engineering, project phasing and a new financial partner, with a new Schedule of Performance due before the period ends around April 2027). No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's own last_verified date.

facts.value: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP)

As last formally endorsed (2022, never executed): approximately 215,000 sq ft office, up to 20,000 sq ft retail, approximately 130,000 sq ft public access/open space; cost estimate approximately $528-536 million, up from an original approximately $383 million 2020 proposal. Explicitly under review ("value engineering", "scope reduction") under the 2026 Amended ENA and not current.

open_questions: No Port Commission agenda item after 2026-04-28 was found; the 12-month Evaluation Period runs to approximately April 2027 with an interim Schedule of Performance due before then -- worth a periodic re-check rather than treating April 2026 as the final word.
No current, authoritative square footage or cost figure exists for the project as of this record's last_verified date: the 2022 estimates are explicitly being re-evaluated under the 2026 Amended ENA.

No public official's or community/maritime-advocacy group's position on the 2026 Amended ENA or settlement specifically has been found and sourced (all community-input coverage found dates to the 2020 RFP era).

Given the project's history of default and its ongoing, unresolved Evaluation Period, its ultimate outcome is genuinely uncertain -- this record treats it as an active but fragile project worth continued tracking, not a settled one.

record.notes: The 2022 scope estimate (~215,000 sq ft office, up to 20,000 sq ft retail, ~$528-536M cost) is explicitly under review ('value engineering', 'scope reduction') per the April 2026 Amended ENA and is not treated as current. Separately, an August 2026 marketing listing ('Pacific Cornerstone') offers up to ~279,876 sq ft of the piers for long-term lease to credit tenants, positioning occupancy for late 2029 -- parallel tenant-marketing activity alongside the Port's own Evaluation Period, not a confirmed deal.
